name: Difference in differences

subjectOf.text: Difference-in-differences analysis confirms the regression discontinuity results, showing a positive and highly significant treatment coefficient for funds above the $150 million AUM threshold.
subjectOf.abstract: Our DiD analysis confirms the results of our RD design. Table 9 shows the dummy variable that identifies the treatment with a positive coefficient that is highly significant.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: treatment defined as AUM above $150 million after March 2012

subjectOf.text: The difference-in-differences interaction term identifying treated funds in 2012 is positive and statistically significant in March, April, and May 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: Table 9 also shows that the dummy variable that identifies the treatment group univocally (year 2012 and AUM>150M) is positive and statistically significant in March, April and May 2012.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: post reform dummy interacted with the AUM above $150 million dummy

subjectOf.text: The difference-in-differences treatment effect is unstable over time: it loses significance in June and July 2012, then becomes significant again in August and September 2012 with negative coefficients and in October 2012 with a positive coefficient.
subjectOf.abstract: It loses significance in June and July, but it becomes significant again in August, September (with a negative coefficient) and October (with a positive coefficient).
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: monthly DiD regressions March to October 2012

subjectOf.text: The parallel trends assumption required for the difference-in-differences design is satisfied, because pre-treatment performance data show the same time trends for treatment and control groups.
subjectOf.abstract: Using additional pre-treatment performance data, Figure 13 suggests that the trends in our dataset are the same for the treatment and control group.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: treatment and control defined by the $150 million AUM threshold
